summary.text: PVDF is polyvinylidene fluoride, a semicrystalline polymer that carries light load well above its glass transition. Makers sell it for electrical and electronic equipment and demanding applications, citing resistance to most chemicals and solvents, and a maker does not recommend food contact. On the H2C it prints at 250⁠–⁠265 °C, and a maker recommends a heated chamber but says no drying is needed.

items.text: Rated for uses up to 130C – this filament can be used in demanding applications under the most extreme conditions.
PVDF is resistant to most chemicals and solvents, making it a great fit for applications which will be exposed to harsh environments.
Excellent resistance to a broad range of chemicals, such as automotive fluids, oils, gas, lubricants, fully halogenated hydrocarbons, alcohols, acids, and bases
Inherently UV-resistant with very stable H-F bonds.
Low smoke and flame characteristics with a base resin rated V-0
Very good abrasion resistance – similar to Nylon and UHMW-PE for high-wear applications
PVDF [Polyvinylidene fluoride] is a high-performance polymer which offers exceptional thermal and chemical resistances.
Non-hygroscopic, does not absorb moisture. No drying needed!
This material can be used for production of electrical and electronic equipment.

items.text: Its chemical structure, fluor atoms in the polymer chain, and high crystallinity make it extremely mechanically resistant, exceptionally chemically resistant, weather-resistant, and much more.
Thanks to a strong H–F bond, the polymer chains can’t be easily attacked and influenced even by harsh chemicals, or moisture.
Certain chemical substances have no influence on Fluorodur up to temperatures about 100–140 °C. But it always depends on different parameters.
The usage for food contact application is not recommended.
